answer: Each new identity is filed via a sponsor sonnet sheet for its work and rung. It locks a 70-credit bond sealed by a plume mark binding sponsor and identity; an auditor checks sheet, seal, and rung, and a reused seal or skipped rung burns bonds. The first filing costs 32, the kth on the spiral costs 32+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8024 and 1000 fakes cost 4,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. New sponsors inherit the rung, so splitting cannot reset price; a rented-sponsor ring fails because shared seals cluster. An honest identity pays 32 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
